rl_causeway.name: The Causeway
rl_causeway.desc: A line of posts, each with a lamp-hook, leads across the black water to a tower: the keeper's last mile. The fog stands behind you like a wall, and ahead the reeds have been cut back, once, by someone who meant the path to last.

features.posts|hooks|hook: Every hook is polished by years of someone's hand. Every lamp is gone.
features.fog|wall: White on the water, and quite still. From this side it looks like a sheet hung out to dry.

rl_sluice.name: The Sluice Works
rl_sluice.desc: Gears and a rusted wheel: the tide-gate that made the ferry channel. Brine drips from the gantry and the whole works ticks softly, like a clock that has forgotten what it is counting.

features.wheel|gears|gate: It turns a quarter-turn when the tide moves, as it was built to.
features.gantry: A plank walk over the gate. Chalked on a beam: LAMPS OUT AT SUNRISE. Nobody has rubbed it off, and nobody has had a sunrise to obey it.

rl_tower_foot.name: The Tower Foot
rl_tower_foot.desc: Two hundred steps spiral up a wall of white-washed stone, each with a chalk tally. The door at the foot of the stair is shut, and the whitewash round it is the only clean thing in the marsh.

n.msg: The tower door is locked. The keeper kept his key where he kept the oil, in the oil-house south of the sluice, and the oil-house has guests.

features.tally|steps|stair: Ansel counted his own steps. The last tally is dated the night he came down for the Keeper.
features.door: Oak, banded with brass gone green. There is a small notch worn in the sill where a boot waited for the lock, every dusk, for years.

rl_lantern_room.name: The Lamp Room
rl_lantern_room.desc: A room of glass, open to the sky where the panes have fallen. The great lens-cradle stands empty in the middle of the floor, with a nest of grey plumes under it, where the keeper used to stand to trim the flame. Far below, the black marsh goes on in every direction.

fixed.intro: The heron does not move. Only her eye turns, slowly, and the sliver of lens in it finds your lantern.

features.cradle: Brass, bent at one corner where something heavy was lifted out in a hurry.
features.plumes|heap: A heap of grey plumes under the cradle, nested into a bed. Under them, glints of glass.
features.pole: The keeper's snuffing-pole, laid in among the plumes where the heron's bed took it in, brass tip toward the ceiling.

rl_cottage.name: The Keeper's Cottage
rl_cottage.desc: A keeper's cottage, tidy, cold. A kettle on the stove, a cot made up with a blanket folded square, and a lantern bracket by the door worn bright by a hand that reached for it every dusk. It is the only room in the marsh that feels expected.
rl_cottage.wake: You wake on the keeper's cot with the kettle singing. Nobody is there. Your purse is lighter by %d gold. The second cup has been moved an inch toward you.
rl_cottage.waypost_text: {amber}On the porch a small waypost lantern hangs where the keeper's own once hung. You trim its wick and touch your flame to it. It catches, and for a moment you think you hear a kettle begin to sing.{/}

features.kettle|cups|cup: Two cups. One is clean. One has a ring of tea gone to stone.
features.cot|blanket: Made up for someone who would be back by dawn. The blanket is folded in thirds, the way a man folds it who is used to having nobody to tell.

rl_oilhouse.name: The Oil-House
rl_oilhouse.desc: Barrels of whale oil, still sweet, stacked to the rafters in the cool. Drip-trays, funnels and a tally board on the wall. Whatever else has gone wrong with the Reedlight, someone kept the books on the oil.

fixed.intro: The keeper's drowned assistants look up from the barrels, lamp-hooks in their hands. They are still on shift.

features.barrels|oil: Stamped REEDLIGHT. Not one has leaked in fifty years.
features.board|tally: The oil ledger, in two hands. The newer hand stops mid-line, on a Tuesday. The older hand has written underneath it, very neatly, 'Gone to fetch the Keeper.'
